title: First-Year Success & Benefits Roadmap
author: Rachel Kim
content:
Overview

This playbook is a consolidated guide for new Redwoood employees and managers to help the first year be predictable, growth-oriented, and well-supported. It bundles practical onboarding checkpoints, a high-level view of role families and promotion expectations, an executive summary of benefits and key perks, and a pragmatic tools & access checklist for hands-on setup. Use this as the single-source starting point for new-joiner planning; links at the end point to deeper operational pages.

Principles
- Clear milestones: Day 1, 30, 90, 6 months, 1 year with measurable outcomes.
- Manager + peer partnership: managers own calibration and goal-setting, peers own project integration.
- Reduce cognitive load: ship minimal viable access and tooling on Day 1.
- Growth-first culture: promotion readiness is based on demonstrated impact, not tenure.

Quick start summary (one-line)
- Before start: complete preboarding forms, read Code of Conduct, submit hardware preferences.
- Day 1: Slack account, laptop, SSO, HR orientation, manager 30/90 plan.
- 30 days: first project deliverable, working in repo, basic observability dashboards accessible.
- 90 days: project ownership, 1:1 cadence established, mid-probation check.
- 1 year: promotion review eligibility conversation if impact and competencies align.

Getting ready (pre-boarding checklist)
1) HR tasks (before start): complete I-9 / local tax forms, sign offer, designate emergency contact.
2) Hardware request: choose Mac/Linux workstation or request a GPU laptop (approval needed for research roles).
3) Training assignments: read Security Acceptable Use, internal API standards, and Privacy & Data Handling.
4) Access requests: submit SSO access ticket (include manager and team name).

Day 1 (manager checklist)
- Welcome and orientation: 30–45 minute welcome call; provide team org chart, key contacts, and the 30/90 day plan document.
- Setup: verify laptop build, VPN & SSO, Slack, Google Workspace, GitHub access, Jira access, Confluence access.
- Role clarity: walk through team goals, expected first project, and cadence for 1:1s.

30/60/90 milestone template (to be kept in the employee's private onboarding doc)
- 30 days (getting started): can run local dev environment, submits first PR, completed at least two onboarding trainings.
- 60 days (contribute): leads a small feature or bug fix, demonstrates understanding of service boundaries and SLOs.
- 90 days (ownership): owns a customer-facing or internal feature, presents a short demo at team retro, probation review completed.

Role families and promotion primer
- Role families at a glance: IC Software Engineers, ML Engineers, Infra & SRE, Product, Design, Research, People Ops, Sales & CS.
- Leveling snapshot (high-level):

| Level | Scope | Typical signals for promotion |
|-------|-------|------------------------------|
| L1-L2 | Learning & delivery | Consistent ticket throughput, strong fundamentals, code reviews with guidance |
| L3 | Independent contributor | Leads features end-to-end, mentors juniors, reliable cross-team communication |
| L4 | Senior / cross-team impact | Designs systems, sets API/infra standards, measurable product outcomes |
| L5+ | Staff / Principal | Shapes roadmap, leads multi-team initiatives, influences hiring and architecture |

- Promotion process summary: manager raises case, peer references collected, promotion packet prepared (impact writeup + artifacts), calibration panel (quarterly) makes decision. See related page for full Leveling rubric.

Benefits & perks — executive summary
- Health & wellness: comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans; 401(k) with company match (US), country-specific retirement options in EMEA/APAC.
- Time off: flexible PTO policy (manager-approved), 12 paid holidays, 8-week paid parental leave (primary caregiver), caregiver leave and top-up options.
- Stipends & allowances: home office stipend at onboarding ($650 USD), continuous learning stipend ($1,200/year), conference budget (manager-approved).
- Financial & equity: competitive salary bands, annual performance bonus (eligible after 6 months), equity grants for full-time employees.
- Perks: monthly wellness allowance, commuter subsidy (where available), catered team lunches + in-office snacks, and employee referral bonus.

How to use benefits (practical steps)
1) Enroll in health plans within 30 days of start; HR will provide the enrollment packet and vendor links.
2) Submit home office stipend via internal expenses form (Finance -> Expenses -> Home Office).
3) Request learning reimbursements: attach course receipt and manager approval to the learning expense form.

Tools & access (practical)
- Identity & SSO: Okta is the company SSO. MFA (YubiKey or Authenticator) is required for elevated roles.
- Communication: Slack (primary), bi-weekly All-Hands, team retros. Use #team-{name} and #prod-incidents channels for signal routing.
- Repo & code reviews: GitHub org: redwood-inference. Default branching: main protected; PR reviews require two approvers for L3+ code.
- Issue tracking: Jira projects by team (project keys are in the team intro doc).
- CI/CD & deployment: Buildkite for pipelines; use PR templates and pre-merge checks.
- Product & infra consoles: Redwood Console (internal) for observability; internal Grafana dashboards share SLOs.

Sample access escalation flow
1) New hire lacks GitHub access: manager opens Support ticket: #access-requests and tags infra-oncall.
2) Tier 1 (IT) verifies employment status and Okta account.
3) Tier 2 (Platform team) grants repo membership and deploy keys.
4) Expected resolution SLA: 48 hours for standard requests, 8 hours for high-priority (release-blocking).

Performance, feedback, and development
- 1:1 cadence: recommended weekly for first 90 days, then at least biweekly. 1:1s should include agenda, progress against learning goals, and blockers.
- Performance reviews: 6-month probation check, then annual performance review with midpoint check. Promotion windows are quarterly; readiness can be submitted any time but should align with quarterly calibrations.
- Career planning: employees and managers build an Individual Development Plan (IDP) every 6 months; learning stipend usage should be tracked there.

Hiring & interviewing — best practices for managers
- Interview panel: include at least one peer from the hiring team and one cross-functional interviewer. Use the structured rubric (behavioral + technical + role-specific).
- Offer timeline: aim to make an offer within two weeks of final interview; update Recruiting when deviating.
- Onboarding handoff: Hiring manager fills the Hiring -> Onboarding Form (link in related pages) with project, mentor, and hardware notes 2 days before start.

Templates and checklists (links and samples)
- 30/90 plan template: create in employee’s private Confluence page and share with manager.
- Preboarding email template: provided in HR -> Templates.
- Manager first-week checklist: quick checklist to confirm access, 1:1 schedule, intro meetings.

Escalations & expected SLAs
- HR policy questions: People Ops triage in 24–48 hours.
- Security / data incidents: follow the Incident Response Security runbook (link in related pages) and notify Security within 1 hour.
- Payroll & compensation corrections: Finance triage within 3 business days.

Appendix: example 30/90 goals (text table)
| Goal phase | Concrete example goal | Success metric |
|------------|----------------------|----------------|
| 30 days | Run dev environment & ship bug fix | PR merged, CI green, deployed to staging |
| 60 days | Deliver a minor feature and own rollout | Feature flag enabled, metrics tracking in Grafana |
| 90 days | Present project and handoff doc | Demo given, runbook created, peer signoff |

End of document
